Improve photographic quality without redesigning her appearance or making her slimmer/younger. Keep her actual concentrated writing expression.
Image 2: composition/finish guide ONLY, NOT a face reference. Use a similar close waist-up 4:3 framing and visual scale, with head at upper-right, hands and document at lower-left, grey chair at right, warm cream marble room and muted berry accents. DO NOT copy the invented woman's facial features from image 2.
Image 3: original portrait of the woman from image 1, supporting her exact identity if needed.
Reframe the real writing scene from image 1 into this close landscape crop, clean up the ring-light reflections on the marble wall, give it soft flattering but natural studio lighting, warm cream color grading and high detail. Preserve the real person's facial/profile structure from image 1 rather than synthesizing a generic cosmetologist. Calm editorial salon photography; avoid glamour retouching, exaggerated eyelashes, altered anatomy, new objects or text. Landscape 4:3, 1448x1086.
post_edit: Lower the writing elbow next to the torso, relax the shoulder and rest the forearm naturally on the desk.
post_edit_prompt:
Precisely edit ONLY the woman's WRITING ARM in this photograph: her right arm, which reaches toward image-left and holds the blue pen.
Lower that elbow significantly and bring it inward next to her waist, instead of holding the arm extended out to the side. The upper arm should descend naturally beside the torso from a relaxed, lowered shoulder. Bend the elbow comfortably around a right angle near the table edge, and let the forearm rest on the tabletop, extending diagonally toward the writing hand and document. The elbow must no longer look raised or floating. Reconstruct the white sleeve folds to follow this relaxed seated writing posture, with continuous plausible shoulder–upper arm–elbow–forearm anatomy. Keep the pen tip touching the paper; preserve the writing hand and fingers as closely as the corrected posture allows.
Lock her face, identity, downward gaze, head angle, hair, torso, other supporting arm and hand, paper, desk, chair, room, camera angle, zoom, lighting and warm colors. Change only the writing-arm posture and its necessary sleeve folds. Natural unposed human posture, same 4:3 photograph.
